---
title: "Mathematics PhDs in Europe"
subtitle: "A public notebook of official data"
---

I have a mathematics PhD and I teach in a high school. This site is my public notebook of what official statistics actually record about mathematics and statistics doctorates in Europe — how many are awarded, and, for Italy only so far, what jobs they hold.

It is not a forecast of your career, and it does not invent an EU job-market average.

## What is here

- **[Supply](supply.qmd)** — Eurostat counts of doctoral degrees in *Mathematics and statistics* (ISCED-F 2013 `F054`), by country, year, and sex.
- **[Italy](italy.qmd)** — AlmaLaurea employment outcomes for **scienze di base** (basic sciences), the official closest field. Not mathematics-only.
- **[Methods](methods.qmd)** — definitions, exclusions, and why some familiar headlines are missing.
- **[Downloads](downloads.qmd)** — the same CSV files the pages use.

## What is not here

No EU employment rate, salary, or gender-gap figure. Those series are not published on a common definition for mathematics PhDs, and this site will not blend national surveys into one.

No machine-learning forecasts, no policy scenarios, no map of “job prospects.”

## How this grows

A new country or a new official table becomes a new folder under `data/` and a new page. Modules stay side by side. They are not averaged together later unless the series are definition-matched and we say so explicitly.
